title: A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators (Mirek–Thiele), formalized in Lean 4
abstract: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the three main theorems of M. Mirek and C. Thiele, "A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators", Proc. London Math. Soc. 114 (2017): the perfect multilinear local T(1) theorem (Theorem 1.3), the perfect multilinear local T(b) theorem with general testing functions on admissible collections of paths (Theorem 1.4), and the perfect multilinear global T(b) theorem (Theorem 1.11), for n-linear forms on dyadic test functions in R^d satisfying the dyadic decay, perfect smoothness and qualitative truncation conditions. The development follows the paper's proof of Theorem 1.4 (stopping times, pruning, the telescoping identities, the discrete Carleson embedding and the outer-measure Hölder inequalities of Do–Thiele, the contraction step and its iteration) and the global/local reduction of Theorem 1.11, including the atom estimate for the dyadic Hardy norm for all exponents (Burkholder's L^p bound for the dyadic square function by Marcinkiewicz interpolation). Theorem 1.3, cited as folklore in the paper, is proved by a dyadic paraproduct argument with a dyadic John–Nirenberg inequality for the paraproduct symbols. All constants depend only on the dimension, the linearity, the testing constant and the exponents.
